newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich Court upholds UBS share plan.
newsitem.headline: Zurich Court upholds UBS share plan.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said the commercial court of Zurich had upheld the bank's plan to introduce a single bearer share and if no appeals against the ruling were filed within one month, the single share would be introduced "immediately."
In addition to the two suits calling for annulment, BK Vision has filed a suit alleging criminal charges against UBS management and a civil suit against the board of directors.
The UBS spokeswoman, however, said these other suits do not affect the decision to introduce a single share.
A statement by UBS said the Zurich commercial court had completely rejected the allegations by BK Vision in connection with the introduction of a single share.
The court confirmed that UBS was correct in the way it acted regarding proxy voting rights, UBS said.
The court also examined the issue of voting rights attached to shares bought on a forward basis.
"It is very positive that in the well-known Kipp case the court said we acted correctly and the deal was done at market prices," the UBS spokeswoman said.

The main issue in BK Vision's action for annulment was whether shares bought by a UBS subsidiary from Karl Heinz Kipp -- a wealthy German living in Switzerland -- on a forward basis for delivery after the shareholders' meeting could be voted by Kipp.
The court ruled that there was no proof of an agreement of how to vote at the shareholders' meeting and the owner of the shares, Kipp, was therefore entitled to vote.
"The person who is a shareholder at the time of the shareholders' meeting is entitled to vote," UBS said.

"UBS is extremely satisfied that there is a clear and substantial decision in the important conflict over the introduction a unitary share. UBS hopes to be able to introduce the unitary share as soon as possible," UBS said.
